# caption

**In one sentence:** draws the one-line "model status" readout (loading, device, elapsed time, weights loaded, progress bar) that model-backed steps show while they work.

## Why it exists
Loading a captioning or image model can take minutes. The job sends a `caption_status` object while that happens, and this folder turns it into readable text so the user can see it is not stuck.

## What's inside
| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `status.js` | `renderCaptionStatus(element, status)` fills or hides a status element; `formatElapsed(seconds)` gives `48s` / `10m 12s`. Private helpers build the "Weights 6.2 / 9.4 GB · 66%" line and the progress bar. |

## How it works
- No status or no `phase` → the element is hidden and emptied.
- Line 1: message (or phase) plus adapter / device / quantization and elapsed time.
- Optional lines: weights loaded vs total (only when both byte counts are known), a `detail` line, and a progress bar (only for a real 0–1 fraction).
- The element gets `data-phase` so CSS can style it (e.g. red when `failed`).

## Who uses it
- `job/view.js` — the status line under the current step in the main window.
- `steps/bbox_annotation/bbox_annotation.js`, `steps/caption_verify/caption_verify.js` — the same line inside their modals.
- `steps/caption_verify/components/preview.js` — uses `formatElapsed` only.

## Good to know
- The `caption-status__*` styles live in `job/job.css`, `steps/bbox_annotation/bbox_annotation.css`, and `steps/caption_verify/caption_verify.css`, not here.
- Time and size formats mirror Python's `load_status` helpers so the CLI and UI read the same.
